tab2_finance.headline: Markets Mixed as U.S.-Israel War on Iran Spooks Investors
tab2_finance.summary: S&P 500 ended +0.1%, Nasdaq +0.4%, Dow -0.2% on Monday. Oil surged ~8% to $72.50/bbl after Iran claimed to close the Strait of Hormuz. Defense stocks (NOC +6%, RTX +4.7%, LMT +3.4%) and oil majors rallied while airlines and cruise lines plunged.

tab2_finance.headline: Gold Hits $5,335/oz — Safe-Haven Demand Surges
tab2_finance.summary: Gold futures advanced nearly 2% to $5,335/oz amid Middle East conflict, approaching January's record above $5,625. Treasury yields rose to 4.05% on the 10-year note, up from 3.95% Friday. Bitcoin recovered to $69,200 after dipping to $63,000 over the weekend.

tab2_finance.headline: 401(k) Limit Rises to $24,500 in 2026 — Max Out Now
tab2_finance.summary: The 2026 annual 401(k)/403(b) contribution limit increased from $23,500 to $24,500. IRA limits also updated. Catch-up contributions for ages 60–63 rise to $11,250. Tax season refunds are running 13–14% higher year-over-year — consider directing refunds to retirement accounts.

tab2_finance.headline: Supreme Court Rules IEEPA Does Not Authorize Presidential Tariffs
tab2_finance.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled on Feb 20, 2026 that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does NOT authorize the president to impose tariffs. Trump's new 10% global import tariff is now under legal challenge. Markets are watching for economic ripple effects on consumer prices.

tab2_finance.headline: AI Disruption Hammers Software & Data Stocks — Opportunity or Trap?
tab2_finance.summary: AI disruption fears have sent software, logistics, financial data, and wealth management stocks down 25–60% from recent highs. Carnegie Invest notes markets are 'selling first, asking questions later.' Investors should distinguish between structural decline and temporary repricing.

tab2_finance.headline: 6 Best Places to Put Your Money in March 2026
tab2_finance.summary: Financial pros recommend: (1) Short-term CDs for locked-in yields, (2) High-yield savings accounts (up to 4.00% APY), (3) ETFs/mutual funds in defensive sectors, (4) Global equities for diversification, (5) TIPS for inflation protection, (6) Short-duration bond funds for stability.

tab2_finance.headline: U.S. Economy Grew Just 1.4% in Q4 2025 — Fed Eyes Rate Cuts
tab2_finance.summary: GDP growth came in weaker than expected at 1.4% annualized in Q4 2025, dragged by a 17% annualized decline in federal government spending. The 2-year Treasury yield has fallen to 2022 lows, signaling bond markets anticipate Fed rate cuts. Inflation from tariffs has been more muted than feared (~2%).

tab2_finance.headline: 68% of Individual Investors Expect Stock Market Gains in 2026
tab2_finance.summary: A new Motley Fool survey finds nearly 70% of individual investors expect positive stock market returns in 2026, with almost no one predicting a correction. Despite Middle East conflict and AI disruption fears, investor sentiment remains broadly bullish — though expectations are modest.

tab3_usGov.headline: U.S. and Israel Launch Major Military Strike on Iran
tab3_usGov.summary: Early Saturday, U.S. and Israeli forces launched a full-scale military assault on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, Iran's defense minister, IRGC chief, and hundreds of civilians. Trump said the operation could last 4–5 weeks. Iran retaliated with drone and missile strikes across the Middle East.

tab3_usGov.headline: Congress Debates War Powers Resolution After Iran Strikes
tab3_usGov.summary: Trump launched strikes without congressional approval, sparking a bipartisan debate. Democrats question the legality of the action; most GOP lawmakers back the president. Congress is expected to consider a War Powers Resolution this week. Strikes came just as Omani mediators announced a diplomatic breakthrough.

tab3_usGov.headline: DHS Partial Government Shutdown Continues — Workers Miss Pay
tab3_usGov.summary: The Department of Homeland Security remains shut down amid a White House-Democrat impasse over ICE funding. Tens of thousands of federal employees — including TSA workers — are missing paychecks. Republicans are using the Iran conflict to pressure Democrats into passing a DHS funding bill.

tab3_usGov.headline: Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump's Tariff Authority Under IEEPA
tab3_usGov.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled on Feb 20 that the president cannot impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Trump's 10% global import tariff is now legally contested. The USTR delivered the 2026 Trade Policy Agenda to Congress on March 2.

tab3_usGov.headline: DOGE Cuts Face Deadline: Congress Must Codify $9.4B in Savings by July 18
tab3_usGov.summary: Lawmakers have until July 18 to pass $9.4 billion in DOGE-driven spending cuts into law. Several GOP senators are expressing skepticism. DOGE activities are now moving to the department and agency level, with scrutiny on federal spending expected to continue throughout 2026.

tab3_usGov.headline: Trump Calls for Regime Change in Iran; Vows Continued Operations
tab3_usGov.summary: In a video message, President Trump called for Iranians to overthrow their government and confirmed 4 U.S. service members have been killed. He said operations could last weeks and the U.S. has the 'capability to go far longer.' Iran's FM condemned the U.S. for abandoning diplomacy mid-negotiation.

tab3_usGov.headline: White House Opposes Utah AI Bill, Pushes Federal AI Authority
tab3_usGov.summary: The White House is opposing state-level AI regulation, including a Utah AI bill, as part of a broader push to centralize federal authority over AI governance. ALEC is urging states to adopt a 'light-touch' approach. The Trump administration's AI agenda aims to prevent a patchwork of state laws.

tab3_usGov.headline: Trump Administration Withdraws from Dozens of International Organizations
tab3_usGov.summary: The Trump administration has withdrawn the U.S. from dozens of international organizations and treaties in an unprecedented move. Legal scholars note a future president could rejoin most of them. The withdrawals are part of a broader 'America First' foreign policy realignment.

tab4_international.headline: U.S.-Israel Strike Kills Iran's Supreme Leader; 550+ Civilians Dead
tab4_international.summary: The joint U.S.-Israeli assault on Iran killed Supreme Leader Khamenei, his daughter, granddaughter, Iran's defense minister, IRGC chief, and 550+ civilians including 165 children in a school strike. Iran launched retaliatory drone and missile attacks across Israel and Gulf Arab nations.

tab4_international.headline: Iran Retaliates: Missiles Hit Israel, Gulf States; Strait of Hormuz Threatened
tab4_international.summary: Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel (killing 9 in Beit Shemesh), struck Gulf Arab nations hosting U.S. bases, and claimed to close the Strait of Hormuz — through which 25% of the world's seaborne oil passes. Qatar halted LNG production. Oil surged 8%, natural gas +3.25%.

tab4_international.headline: European Markets Slump as Iran 'War Trade' Joins AI Disruption Fears
tab4_international.summary: European stocks opened sharply lower Monday as crude oil prices surged. Gulf stock exchanges remained closed. The Iran conflict threatens to push up inflation and dent Europe's already meagre economic growth. The ECB faces new pressure as energy costs rise.

tab4_international.headline: Ukraine Gained More Territory Than It Lost in February 2026
tab4_international.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi announced that Ukrainian forces captured more territory in February than Russia occupied in the same period. The Kremlin says continuing peace talks is in Russia's own interests. Ukraine is also offering to help shoot down Iranian drones used by Russia.

tab4_international.headline: China's CCP Updates Taiwan Policy in New Five-Year Plan (2026–2030)
tab4_international.summary: China's Communist Party has changed how it discusses Taiwan policy in its new Five-Year Plan, with experts saying the approach will become more 'standardized.' Taiwan's MOFA rebuked China's embassy in Israel for offering to evacuate Taiwanese citizens under Chinese travel documents.

tab4_international.headline: UN Nuclear Watchdog Urges Restraint; Natanz Facility Hit
tab4_international.summary: Iran's Natanz nuclear facility was struck during the U.S.-Israeli assault, according to Iran's ambassador to the IAEA. The UN nuclear watchdog urged restraint and called for protection of nuclear sites. The IAEA is monitoring the situation amid fears of radioactive contamination.

tab4_international.headline: Samsung Unveils Galaxy AI Ecosystem Advances at MWC 2026
tab4_international.summary: Samsung showcased the Galaxy S26 series and expanded Galaxy AI ecosystem at Mobile World Congress 2026 in Barcelona. The company is advancing connected device intelligence, AI-powered photography, and cross-device integration. MWC 2026 is packed with major tech announcements.

tab4_international.headline: Europe Debates Sending Troops to Ukraine Without Russian Approval
tab4_international.summary: European leaders are debating whether to send peacekeeping troops to Ukraine without first seeking Russian approval. The Atlantic Council argues Europe must act independently. Discussions are ongoing as the Russia-Ukraine conflict enters a potential ceasefire negotiation phase.

tab5_ai.headline: Amazon Invests $50B in OpenAI in Landmark Strategic Partnership
tab5_ai.summary: Amazon and OpenAI announced a multi-year, $50 billion strategic partnership on Feb 27, 2026. AWS will serve as the exclusive third-party cloud distribution for OpenAI and will consume 2 gigawatts of Trainium capacity. OpenAI also raised $110B in new funding and expanded its AWS agreement to $138B total over 8 years.

tab5_ai.headline: OpenAI Launches Codex-Spark: 1,000+ Tokens/Second Coding Model
tab5_ai.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, a speed-first coding model generating over 1,000 tokens per second with ultra-low latency for real-time interactive coding. It's designed for throughput-heavy coding workflows. GPT-5.1 is being retired on March 11 as GPT-5.2 becomes the flagship model.

tab5_ai.headline: GPT-5.3 Spotted on Chatbot Arena Under Codenames 'Vortex' and 'Zephyr'
tab5_ai.summary: Two mystery OpenAI models appeared on LMSYS Chatbot Arena under codenames 'Vortex' and 'Zephyr,' widely believed to be GPT-5.3. GPT-5.2 is currently the flagship model with state-of-the-art reasoning, long-context understanding, coding, and vision capabilities. GPT-5.1 retires March 11.

tab5_ai.headline: Google DeepMind CEO: AI Hardware Shortages Are Slowing Research
tab5_ai.summary: Demis Hassabis told CNBC that shortages in GPU memory, graphics processing units, and electricity are constraining AI research and deployment. DeepMind is 'lucky' to own TPUs, but hardware bottlenecks remain a systemic challenge across the industry. This is slowing the pace of AI breakthroughs.

tab5_ai.headline: White House Pushes Federal AI Authority; Opposes State-Level Patchwork
tab5_ai.summary: The White House is actively opposing state AI bills (including Utah's) to centralize federal AI regulation. ALEC urges states to adopt 'light-touch' regulation. The Fed is also racing to understand AI's impact on jobs and inflation. BofA economists say AI will create new job types rather than simply eliminate roles.
